title: Included and You-bring lists run off the right edge
what: On all five SRS pages at 1440 px, the Included, You bring, Safety and Organisation lines are one unbroken line that is cut off at the right edge, mid-word ('TASKIN', 'THIRD-PA', 'TRACKLOGS MAN'). Half of each list cannot be read, and body overflow-x:hidden hides the scrollbar, so nothing hints at the missing text.
why: This is a visible build bug, which reads as an unchecked generated page. SailGP never cuts text off: each schedule and info line wraps inside its column.
fix: In words() add spaces around the separator (' / ', as build_bwo.py already does) so the line can wrap between items. Better still, replace these runs with a plain two- or three-column list (see ev-10).

title: The same glider rule is printed on every round, and it is wrong for some
what: Every SRS page says 'Sports class: EN-C and below, including 2-liner Cs. No CCC or EN-D' and lists 'EN-C or below'. On the Krushevo page this contradicts the official listing ('EN-D & below allowed, CCC prohibited'). Lijak's listing says 'CSC wings only', and St André lists no class rule. The You-bring list is also a hard-coded list of 10 items, the same on every page.
why: Boilerplate pasted into every page is a classic generated-content tell, and here it gives a pilot wrong entry rules. SailGP event pages carry event-specific facts only.
fix: Take the allowed-class line from the scraped summary for each round (the ✅/❌ lines next to 'FAI Status'). Build You bring from the scraped REQUIRED list instead of the fixed list. Drop the line where the source says nothing.
where: airtribune-redesign/src/build/build_srs.py:158 short_req() fixed list, airtribune-redesign/src/build/build_srs.py:216 tnote 'Sports class' text

title: '100–120 km' is clipped at phone width
what: At 390 px the Ljubljana distance '100–120 km' runs past the right edge and reads '100–12'. On BWO the Mumbai subline wraps one letter to its own line ('~6 / h').
why: These are unchecked layout breaks. SailGP's mobile info stacks label and value so nothing overflows.
fix: At ≤640 px set .jr .val to font-size 26–28px, or drop the value onto its own row under the city. Write ranges as '100–120' with the unit on the next line. Join '~6 h' with a non-breaking space.

title: 'LIGHTWEIGHT' breaks as 'LIGHTWEIG / HT'
what: At 390 px the Lightweight prize card breaks the word in the middle of a letter pair ('LIGHTWEIG' / 'HT'), and 'MEDIUM WEIGHT' needs two lines in a cramped card.
why: Mid-word breaks are a typical unchecked generated-layout bug. A designer would never ship a split category name.
fix: Remove overflow-wrap:anywhere. Make the categories a single-column typographic list (name left, rule right; see ev-02), or let the name scale down (clamp 16–19px) at ≤640 px.

title: Prize cards still have coloured accent bars on top
what: The four category cards (Overall, Women, Lightweight, Medium weight; on BWO Overall, Female, Sports, British overall) each have a 3px top stripe in a different colour (orange, red, blue, teal). They sit on a frosted gradient card with a big empty middle and one small grey line of text.
why: This is the same 'coloured accent bar' tell the owner already removed from list rows, but in card form. Colour-coding four categories means nothing, and the empty card pattern is template UI. SailGP lists partner tiers as centred text over a thin rule, in one colour.
fix: Remove .prize::before and the four colours. Render the categories as a four-row ruled list: the name in Archivo 800 at about 28px, the eligibility on the same baseline at the right in Inter, with 1px rules between rows. No boxes.

title: Tiny uppercase letter-spaced labels on almost everything
what: Lijak has 56 text elements set as 10–13px uppercase with 0.14–0.18em tracking (BWO has 93). Every h2 has an orange eyebrow over it ('AWARDS' over 'PRIZES & CATEGORIES', 'SPORTS-CLASS RACING SERIES' over 'THE 2027 SEASON', 'FROM THE AIRTRIBUNE ARCHIVE'). Each tab panel opens with a label that repeats the tab name ('ENTRY' under the active ENTRY tab, 'ON SITE' under ON SITE), and each figure has its own orange micro-label.
why: Uppercase 'eyebrow' labels everywhere are the most common generated-UI tell. SailGP uses almost none: the section heading stands alone ('RACING FOR GLORY', 'WEEKEND SCHEDULE'), and labels are plain bold text ('Race Times | 14:00').
fix: Delete every eyebrow over an h2 and every .tb-h row that repeats the tab name. Keep micro-labels only where they name a figure (Entry fee, Field), set them in grey sentence case at 13px with no tracking, and keep orange for one thing only (buttons and active states).

title: The same pink glider fills the hero, intro photo, Race card and season rail
what: On the Lijak page the same pink and yellow canopy appears four times (hero 'pink-blur', intro 'pink-forest', Race card 'pink-close', and the rail card). Every image across the six event pages is one of 8 tight canopy close-ups from Tapalpa (Mexico). None shows the venue, the launch, the town or people.
why: Recycled stock-like crops make the pages feel generated. SailGP's event page uses photos of that venue and of people (fans in the grandstand, boats in front of the city skyline), and no photo repeats on a page.
fix: Use each photo once per page: give each page a distinct set and put a different canopy in the hero than in the intro. Where possible, swap one slot for a wide shot with landscape, take-off or crowd. Caption it honestly ('SRS Tapalpa 2026'), as the footer already does.

title: Six equal stat boxes with placeholder values and a contradiction
what: The band is six identical centred cells: big italic figure, tiny label. On Montclar, Krushevo and St André two cells say 'Soon / ENTRIES OPEN' and '— / COUNTRIES'. On Lijak it reads '100 MAX PILOTS' next to '278 REGISTERED' with no confirmed count (the source has 33 confirmed), so it looks like an error. The 'Registration numbers from Airtribune on 24 Nov 2026.' note floats alone at the right.
why: A row of equal-size stat boxes is a dashboard template. Placeholder cells ('Soon', '—') are empty states pretending to be facts. SailGP's event header gives only date, place and countdown, with no stat strip.
fix: Drop the band or reduce it to facts that exist: 'Entry €320 · Field 100 · 33 confirmed, 278 on the list (24 Nov)'. Set it as one left-aligned typographic line under the hero, and leave out cells with no data rather than printing 'Soon' or a dash.

title: Randomly generated task map with fake terrain
what: The right half of the Flying site tab is a teal contour map from random noise, with a random triangle task ('107.9 km · 3 turnpoints' in a pill), an SSS ring and a goal. A small grey caption admits it is an 'Illustrative task shape, not an official task'. The contours are not Lijak's terrain.
why: Simulated data shown prominently is a strong AI-demo tell: it looks informative but means nothing. SailGP shows a real course or venue map, or a photograph.
fix: Replace it with real information: a static map or satellite crop of the take-off and landing with the two marked (OpenStreetMap or Mapbox static image), or a photo of the launch. If no real data exists, give the column to the site text and drop the task.

title: Lists rendered as slash-separated uppercase italic word runs
what: Included, You bring, Safety, Organisation, Benefits and Environment are each one paragraph of heavy italic caps joined by orange or grey slashes. At 390 px this turns into a 9-line wall of shouting text ('2 M RADIO · 143.900 MHZ', 'EN-C OR BELOW' broken across lines) where items can't be told apart.
why: Slash- and dot-joined word runs used as list styling are a generated-design habit. They make readable checklists into decoration. SailGP lists are plain sentence-case lines ('FAQs ↗', 'Refund Policy ↗').
fix: Make each group a simple list: two or three columns of sentence-case Inter at 15–16px, 8–10px row gap, no separators. Grey and strike-through (or a 'Not provided:' line) for the negative items instead of red caps.

title: Outlined (stroke-only) numerals and codes as decoration
what: Airport codes LJU and VCE, the Included/You bring counts '10', and the BWO years 2025, 2024 and down are drawn as hollow outline text (-webkit-text-stroke). Only the first row is solid orange.
why: Outline display type as a 'premium' accent is a stock template trick and hurts legibility on dark backgrounds. SailGP sets numbers and names solid, in one weight, white on dark.
fix: Set all codes and years solid. If the first row needs emphasis, use white for the first and the grey ink-2 for the rest; no strokes.

title: A big count number beside every list
what: Each list has a big numeral counting its items ('INCLUDED 10', 'YOU BRING 10', 'SAFETY 6', 'BENEFITS 2', 'ENVIRONMENT 1').
why: Counting your own bullet points adds nothing: it is filler to make a row look 'data-rich', and a common generated pattern. SailGP never numbers its lists.
fix: Remove .run-h .n and the counts. Keep the group name as a plain small heading.

title: Giant italic display type on words that aren't figures
what: The 'headline figure' style (Archivo 900 italic, up to 64px) is used for words: 'BORDANO', 'SHUTTLE', 'INCLUDED' (Gemona), 'NOVA GORICA' (Lijak), 'OLA · UBER', 'REDBUS.IN', 'PUNE' (BWO), 'WPRS' (BWO entry).
why: Headline numerals work when they are numbers. A shouted 'INCLUDED' or a website name at poster size reads as filler. SailGP keeps its big type for headings and dates, and practical info is body text.
fix: Use .gs .big only for real numbers (distance, time, price, count). For text answers, put the word in the bold label line ('Practice day shuttle: book via the Navetta VLF Telegram bot') at body size.

title: Italics everywhere, and 46 different type styles
what: Lijak has 91 italic text elements: the hero sub in light italic ('· 15–21 Mar 2027'), the bold italic country, all h3s, band figures, tiles, prize names, list runs, rail dates, airport sublines and photo credits. The page uses 46 distinct size/weight/style combinations (BWO: 49).
why: When everything is slanted, nothing is emphasised, and the type scale looks improvised. SailGP uses italic for two things only (section headings and the date in the event bar), with about 5 type sizes.
fix: Keep italic only for h2/h3 display headings. Make figures, dates, credits and sublines upright. Cut the scale to about 6 steps (e.g. 13, 15, 17, 22, 40, 120+) and map every class onto them.

title: Too many accent colours
what: Next to the orange, the page uses yellow (callout title, 'PARKING'/'SPORTS CLASS' labels, take-off triangle), teal (status chip, map contours, cylinders), the SRS blue-purple-red gradient (WSF chip, quote border), separate red and blue prize stripes, and #FF6B6B for negative items: 9 text colours on the Lijak page.
why: A rainbow of accents with no meaning is a generated look. SailGP is dark green-black, white and one red-orange, with team colours only in flags and logos.
fix: Limit to white, two greys and orange. Make yellow, teal and the SRS gradient plain white or grey. Let SRS colour appear only in its logo.

title: Raw Airtribune date strings, a different format from the rest of the page
what: Edition dates show as '08 - 15 Mar, 2023', '27 Jan, 2024 - 03 Feb, 2024' and '10 - 17 Feb, 2026' (spaced hyphens, leading zeros, repeated year, comma) in light italic. The hero uses '23 Feb – 2 Mar 2027'.
why: Pasted-through source strings show nobody edited the data. SailGP uses one date style everywhere ('28-29 NOVEMBER', '28 - 29 NOV 2026').
fix: Parse when_where into dates and format with the same fmt_dates() rule as the SRS pages ('8–15 Mar 2023', '27 Jan – 3 Feb 2024'). Set them upright.

title: 34 orange T1–T7 tiles turn the history into an admin panel
what: Each edition has a 'TASK REPLAYS' label and a grid of solid orange 40×34px tiles (T1…T7), plus 'Full results ↗'. Across six editions that is 34 orange blocks, the loudest thing on the page.
why: A grid of identical small buttons reads like an admin pagination control, and it puts orange on the least important links. SailGP keeps orange for a few main actions ('BUY TICKETS').
fix: Make the replays a text line: 'Replay  1  2  3  4  5  6  7' in white Inter 600 with tabular numbers, underlined on hover, followed by 'Results ↗'. No fills.

title: Daily schedule boxes are indented 40px and styled like admin chips
what: Under 'DAILY SCHEDULE' the seven times sit in rounded dark boxes in a 2-column grid that starts 40px to the right of the heading (the ul keeps its default padding). The right column has a long empty gap under the links.
why: Misalignment shows nobody checked it, and boxed time chips are dashboard UI. SailGP writes the schedule as text: 'RACE DAY 1 | SATURDAY, 28 NOVEMBER / Race Times | 14:00 - 15:30'.
fix: Add padding:0 to .sched. Render the schedule as a two-column text table (time in tabular figures, then event), with no boxes, or move it under the Event schedule on the right to fill that column.

title: The same buttons repeated up to six times
what: On Lijak 'Register' or 'Details & registration' appears in the nav, hero, Race card, What's on tab and Entry tab, and 'Live tracking' in the hero, Follow live card and What's on tab. The What's on tab repeats the hero's exact orange/outline button pair.
why: Repeating the same CTA pair in every block is a template rhythm. SailGP puts actions where they belong (ticket cards, 'Buy tickets / How to watch' in the info tab) without copying the hero.
fix: Keep the nav Register, the hero pair and the Entry-tab button. Remove the pair from What's on. In the trio cards, use a text link ('Getting there →') instead of three more orange buttons.

title: Boxed frosted fact tiles, with a wrongly uppercased unit
what: Site facts sit in a rounded frosted 2×2 tile grid, each with an eyebrow and a bold italic caps value. CSS uppercasing turns '591 m' into '591 M' (M is mega) and 'Broad grassy slope' into a shouted two-line value.
why: Boxed fact tiles are the card grid the owner moved away from, and the capital unit is a small sign of carelessness. SailGP prints this kind of detail as plain lines.
fix: Make the tiles a two-column definition list on hairline rules (label grey 13px, value white 17px upright). Remove text-transform from values so units stay 'm'.

area: Race / Follow live / Plan your trip cards
title: Generic three-up cards with filler copy
what: Three identical photo cards headed 'RACE', 'FOLLOW LIVE', 'PLAN YOUR TRIP', each with one line and an orange button. 'Follow live' promises 'Every pilot is tracked live… task by task' on a page 111 days before the event. On BWO the Live tracking link is just the event page again.
why: Verb-noun triplets with equal cards are a stock landing-page block. SailGP's three cards are concrete products (ticket types with prices and what you get).
fix: Make the cards concrete or remove them: e.g. 'Entry €320 · 100 places · 33 confirmed', 'Tracking opens on race day 1, 16 Mar', 'Trieste 50 km · Ljubljana 110 km'. Give the follow card no button until there is something live.

title: Glow halos on the tab underline, links and distance dots
what: The active tab underline has a 14px orange glow (box-shadow). Orange links get a text-shadow glow on hover. The distance-bar end dots have a translucent halo ring, and the bars fade from transparent to orange.
why: Neon glows and gradient fills are a generated 'tech' accent. SailGP's active tab is a flat 2px red underline, and its links are plain.
fix: Remove the box-shadow on the tab underline, the link text-shadow, the dot halo and the gradient. Draw a flat 2px orange bar and a flat 8px dot.
where: airtribune-redesign/src/build/srs-template.html:247 tabs ::after box-shadow, :261 .links a:hover text-shadow, :309-310 .jr .track i gradient + ::after halo

title: Stock motion: Ken Burns hero, hover zooms, lifting buttons, fade-ups
what: The hero image slowly zooms out over 26 s. The intro photo, the trio cards and the rail cards zoom on hover. Orange buttons lift 1px (translateY) on hover. Tab panels fade up 8px, the distance bars grow, and the task line draws itself.
why: Motion on every element is the default from generated templates. SailGP's page is static apart from its countdown and carousel arrows.
fix: Keep the tab switch instant (or a plain 150ms opacity). Remove the Ken Burns zoom, the image hover zooms and the button translateY. Leave the colour change on hover only.
where: airtribune-redesign/src/build/srs-template.html:37 .btn-o:hover translateY, :58-59 @keyframes kb, :103 .photo:hover img, :170 .rc:hover img, :236 .pc:hover img, :248-249 .panel fade, :309 track width transition

title: Yellow warning-box callout with bullet dots
what: Special rules sit in a rounded yellow-tinted box with a yellow border, a yellow bold italic caps title and a bulleted list.
why: A tinted alert box is a stock UI component. SailGP would print the rule as text under a heading.
fix: Set it as a plain sub-section: heading 'Local rules' in the h3 style, then a numbered or plain list in body text. No tint, border or yellow.

title: Status pill chip next to the round label
what: The eyebrow 'SRS 2027 · WORLD SPORTS FINAL' is followed by an outlined pill 'CONFIRMED' (teal on most pages, a blue-to-red gradient pill on Gemona, yellow 'PROVISIONAL' on Montclar). The rail has a matching orange 'YOU ARE HERE' pill.
why: Status chips in pastel outlines are generated SaaS UI. SailGP shows status only through its content (dates, countdown).
fix: Show status only when it matters: on Montclar add 'Provisional' as plain grey text after the date ('20–27 Jun 2027 · provisional'). Drop the chip on confirmed rounds. Mark the current rail card with an orange 2px bottom rule instead of a pill.

title: Mixed time formats, uppercased into '1H15'
what: Travel times mix '1h15' (shown as '1H15' because of CSS uppercase), '45′' (prime mark), '1 h 40', '~2 h', '45–60 min' and '20–25 minutes' on the same page.
why: Inconsistent units look machine-assembled. A sports site picks one style and uses it for every number.
fix: Use one format: '1 h 15', '45 min', '2 h'. Remove text-transform:uppercase from .gs .big so units stay lowercase. Use tabular numbers.

title: Slash separators wrap onto the start of lines
what: On BWO the Included and You bring runs wrap so that a line starts with ' / LUNCH PACK', and another line ends with a dangling '/'.
why: Orphaned separators show the list was never set for real line breaks.
fix: This goes away if the runs become real lists (ev-10). Otherwise put the separator inside the preceding nowrap span so it never starts a line.

title: Nations as bare codes with small orange counts, no flags
what: Registrations by nation are bold italic three-letter codes (GBR, USA, FRA…) each followed by a tiny orange number, wrapped in a loose line.
why: Bare codes with superscript-like counts look like a word cloud. SailGP shows nations with real flag images and the name next to them.
fix: Show a ruled list or a 5-column grid: real flag (flag-icons SVG, 20×14), country code, then the count right-aligned in tabular numbers, all white.

title: The event is named three different ways
what: The hero eyebrow says 'British Paragliding Open · 8th edition', while the event is '8th British Winter Open' everywhere else. The prize card says 'Female' and the history rows say 'Women'.
why: Inconsistent naming is a giveaway of assembled copy. SailGP uses one event name throughout.
fix: Use 'British Winter Open · 8th edition' in the hero, and 'Women' in both places (or 'Female' in both).

title: The 5-card rail leaves an orphan card on phones
what: At 390 px the season rail is a 2-column grid of tall rounded cards, so St André sits alone in the last row with an empty slot beside it. Images are dimmed to 55% opacity.
why: An uneven grid with dimmed photos looks templated. SailGP's calendar on mobile is a single horizontal scroller with clear full-colour cards.
fix: At ≤640 px make the rail a horizontal scroll-snap strip (cards at about 70% width), or a one-column text list: round, venue, dates on hairline rules. Show the images at full opacity with a bottom gradient only.
